environment.description: EC2 instance (c5.large) running Amazon Linux 2 in us-east-1, VPC subnet 10.0.2.0/24. The order processor binary is identical. Instance security group allows inbound TCP 8089 from sg-0a3f7c (NLB security group only). A Network Load Balancer (internal, scheme=internal) forwards TCP/8089 to the target group. The NLB has no public DNS and resides in private subnets (10.0.10.0/24, 10.0.11.0/24). A separate Application Load Balancer (internet-facing) on port 443 terminates TLS and forwards to a Lambda authorizer, but does NOT route to this target group. Access to the NLB is gated by VPC routing: the only route to 10.0.10.0/24 and 10.0.11.0/24 is via a Transit Gateway attachment with a prefix list (pl-0x8a4f2e) that resolves to three CIDR blocks: 172.16.0.0/20 (corporate office), 172.16.48.0/22 (warehouse fulfillment systems), and 10.200.0.0/16 (VPN egress for on-prem ERP). The Transit Gateway route table (tgw-rtb-09cf3a) has static routes only for these prefixes with no propagation enabled. There is no internet gateway, NAT gateway, or VPC peering that provides any other ingress path to the NLB subnets. VPC Flow Logs confirm only traffic from these three CIDR ranges has ever reached the NLB listener in the past 90 days.
